To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EMT-mediated increase in mammosphere formation is consistent with a model of CSC enrichment in which pre-existing CSCs are the subjects of accelerated division and increased self-renewal, and that this enrichment is consistent with a lack of perfect biomarkers for mammary (cancers) stem cells.
the EMT can enrich a cell population for cells with a CSC phenotype, and that this enrichment is more pronounced when pre-existing CSCs are targeted.

the induction of epithelial-mesenschymal transition in human breast cancer cells increases stem cell activity as measured by the presence of CD44(high)/ CD24(low) cells, as well as an increase in the number of mammospheres formed, and that this increase can be attributed to a combination of accelerated self-renewing division of pre-existing CSCs and de-differentiation of fully mature cells into a stem cell phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modelling of EMT-mediated cancer stem cell enrichment, a phenomenon which has recently been observed in human mammary carcinoma cell lines.
the mathematical modelling of the relationship between EMT and CSCs.
understanding the relationship between EMT and cancer stem cell activity and with the implications of these findings in the context of cancer metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the evidence for EMT-mediated CSC induction is strong and growing, the exact mechanism by which this occurs remains unclear.

EMT does not necessarily lead to an increase in the number of CSCs, but it may increase their proportion in the cell population, and that the mammosphere data can provide insight into the nature of the CSC hierarchy in mammary carcinomas.
the EMT-CSC link has been shown in vitro, but the mechanism is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of EMT-mediated enrichment of CSCs, the CSCs are not the cells that experience the transition, but instead, they are the cells that benefit the most from the transition.
EMT can be a source of stem cell enrichment in breast carcinoma.
the EMT process is a complex one, and that the CSC phenotype is a complex one as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EMT can indeed increase stemness in a cell population, but the mechanism by which this occurs is highly dependent upon the cell type and context under consideration.
the EMT-mediated increase in CSC activity is not a simple process and may be mediated by a combination of mechanisms, which may vary depending on the cell type and tumour stage.
EMT-mediated CSC induction may not be as dramatic as has been previously suggested.
